SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p777/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p777/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p777/r5.claim: الأبرار is a paucity plural used for believers, while البررة is an abundance plural for angels because they are more numerous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p777/r5.anchor: (الأبرار) جمع قلة وهي تستعمل للمؤمنين فقط (إن الأبرار لفي عليين) و (البررة) جمع كثرة وهي تستعمل للملائكة فقط لأنهم أكثر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r1.claim: The guarded tablet is a priceless divine treasure accessible only by God’s leave and bestowed on the Prophet for the worthy; he should not cast pearls before a swine.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r1.anchor: he should only present it before those who are worthy of it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r2.claim: The guarded tablet is a powerful, priceless treasure protected by angels.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r2.anchor: it is a powerful and priceless treasure

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r3.claim: Ṣaḥīfa means a written page and its plural can mean a book; here it denotes the guarded tablet, a priceless treasure accessible only by God’s leave and bestowed on the Prophet for the worthy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r3.anchor: it refers to the guarded tablet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r4.claim: The pages’ raised quality denotes exalted meaning and status, as in 43:4, which describes the original book as exalted and wise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r4.anchor: The former refers to exaltedness both in meaning and status

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r5.claim: Their purification means the Qur’an is secure from devils; 56:78–79 calls it a guarded book accessible only to the pure, with angels as its trustworthy custodians.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r5.anchor: is to bring to light the fact

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p180/r8.claim: The final adjectives describe the custodians as high-status, honorable, obedient, faithful, responsible, and trustworthy, incapable of dishonesty or allowing devils access.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r1.claim: The messenger delivering revelation is powerful, honored, obeyed, and trustworthy, as described in 81:19–21.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r1.anchor: This is the word brought by a noble messenger; he is endued with great power

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r2.claim: The Qur’an and its custodians’ attributes require the Prophet and his Companions to preach with honor and dignity rather than beg or implore.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r2.anchor: it should be presented with honour and dignity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r3.claim: The archangel and the scribes entrusted with revelation have lofty character and integrity; earthly transmitters are selected for corresponding qualities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p181/r3.anchor: only those people in this earth are selected to transmit and deliver this word of God who have the same qualities and attributes

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.speaker: مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.claim: In a mursal report, Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to be brought near while the Prophet addressed a Meccan notable; the opening was revealed when the Prophet turned toward the notable. Al-Tirmidhi transmits a similar report from Urwa via Aisha and grades it hasan gharib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.anchor: وهو ما رواه مالك في ( الموطأ ) مرسلا عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه أنه قال : أنزلت { عبس وتولى } في ابن أم مكتوم

STUDYQURAN:80:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:15/r3.claim: A famous hadith says that a proficient Quran reciter who has memorized it is with the noble, pious scribes.
STUDYQURAN:80:15/r3.anchor: A famous ḥadīth states, “One who recites the Quran proficiently and has memorized it is with the scribes, noble and pious” (IK)

TAB-FULL:v24p110/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p110/r1.claim: Barara is the plural of barr, like kafara from kafir and sahara from sahir; Arabic normally uses barr and barra as singulars, while plural formation returns to the fa'il pattern. He cites heard forms such as khayr and barr.
TAB-FULL:v24p110/r1.anchor: وقوله: {كرام بررة} [عبس: 16] والبررة: جمع بار، كما الكفرة جمع كافر

TABATABAI:80:13-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r6.claim: Bi-aydī safarah is another adjective of the sheets; safarah means envoys or messengers (singular safīr), while noble describes their persons and virtuous describes their deeds.
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r6.anchor: بأيدي سفرة كرام بررة } صفة بعد صفة لصحف، والسفرة هم السفراء جمع سفير

TABATABAI:80:13-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r7.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder written in multiple honored, elevated, pure sheets, carried by angels noble to God in essence and virtuous in their actions.
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r7.anchor: ومعنى الآيات أن القرآن تذكرة مكتوبة في صحف متعددة معظمة مرفوعة قدرا مطهرا من كل دنس وقذارة بأيدي سفراء من الملائكة كرام على ربهم بطهارة ذواتهم بررة عنده

BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r16.claim: The angels are noble in God's sight through nearness and honor, or gracious toward believers by seeking forgiveness for them.
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r16.anchor: كرام} عند الله بالقرب والشرف فهو من الكرامة جمع كريم أو متعطفين

BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r17.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says their nobility means they do not accompany Adam's descendants during intercourse or while relieving themselves, referring to the angels called noble writers.
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله يريد أنهم يتكرمون أن يكونوا مع ابن آدم

BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r18.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r18.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r18.claim: Barara may mean pious, because the angels transcend materiality and attachments; obedient to God; or truthful in their oaths, from barr in an oath.
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r18.anchor: {بررة} اتقياء لتقدسها عن المواد ونزاهة جواهرها عن التعلقات أو مطيعين

BURHAN:v4p17/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p17/r1.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v4p17/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that angels are called barara, stronger than abrār: barara is the plural of barr, whose sense is stronger than bārr; the distinction assumes angels’ superiority.
BURHAN:v4p17/r1.anchor: قال الراغب فخص ( 3 ) الملائكة بها ( 4 ) من حيث أنه ابلغ

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r22.claim: The angels are noble with God and obediently righteous.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r22.anchor: كرام بررة } . كرام عند الله بررة

ITQAN:v1p125#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p125#2/r5.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
ITQAN:v1p125#2/r5.claim: A group of scholars says the whole Qur’an descended on Laylat al-Qadr from the Preserved Tablet to Bayt al-‘Izza, then Gabriel delivered it to the angelic scribes.
ITQAN:v1p125#2/r5.anchor: قال جماعة من العلماء نزل القرآن جملة في ليلة القدر من اللوح المحفوظ إلى بيت يقال له بيت العزة

ITQAN:v2p565/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p565/r1.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p565/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib says barara, used of angels, is more emphatic than abrār for humans because it is the plural of the stronger form bārr.
ITQAN:v2p565/r1.anchor: ذكره الراغب ووجهه بأن الثاني أبلغ لأنه جمع بار وهو أبلغ من بر مفرد الأول

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r1.claim: The paired lines by al-Buʿayth and al-Buḥturī illustrate patterned borrowing through a shared construction, counted among the refinements of poetic emulation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r1.anchor: وهذا الذي كتبت من حلي الأخذ في الحذو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r2.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r2.claim: Al-ʿAskarī relates that al-Buḥturī saw a formal echo of Abū Kharāsh’s verse in Abū Nuwās’s line even though their meanings differed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r2.anchor: وحكى العسكري في ' صنعة الشعر ' أن ابن الرومي قال : قال لي البحتري : قول أبي نواس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r3.claim: Al-Buḥturī’s line and Abū Tammām’s line each follow al-Farazdaq’s model, another subtle form of poetic emulation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r3.anchor: قد احتذى كل واحد منهما على قول الفرزدق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r4.claim: Dhū al-Rummah says he shaped unusual verses and rhymes without modeling them on anything he had heard.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r4.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة ، + الوافر + :
 ( وشعر قد أرقت له غريب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r5.claim: Simply reciting or reading a poem is not called imitation; replacing each word with a synonym is not poetic emulation either.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r5.anchor: فأما أن يجعل إنشاد الشعر وقراءته احتذاء فمما لا يعلمونه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r6.claim: A synonym-for-synonym rewrite is called slakh, which poets deride and consider a foolish practice.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p339/r6.anchor: ولكن يسمون هذا الصنيع سلخا ، ويرذلونه

DAMGHANI:v1p67/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r3.claim: Barara means those obedient to God; the same sense applies to the record of the righteous.
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r3.anchor: يعني مطيعين لله تعالى . كقوله تعالى في سورة المطففين

AKHFASH:v2p567/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p567/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p567/r2.claim: The singular of barrara is bārr, and barrara is a collective plural of abrār.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.claim: The second sense is obedience, illustrated by cooperation in righteousness, dutifulness to parents, righteous conversation, and the record and character of the righteous angels.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r7.claim: A sixth sense is pious or righteous; the author says it would also be sound to attach this sense to the first category of excellence.

FARRA:v3p236/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p236/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p236/r6.claim: By Arabic analogy, the singular of بررة is بار, since فَعَلة plurals of active participles usually have singulars on فاعل, like كافر/كفرة and فاجر/فجرة.
FARRA:v3p236/r6.anchor: الواحد منهم في قياس العربية بار لأن العرب لا تقول

FARRA:v3p236/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p236/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p236/r7.claim: Actual Arab usage also has رجل بر and امرأة برة, with بررة as a plural construed on the sense of فاعل; he heard قوم خيرة بررة, whose singulars are خير and بر.

FARRA:v3p236/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p236/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p236/r8.claim: In قوم سراة, the expected singular would be ساريا, but Arabs use سري; they pluralize a sāri as سراة/غزاة with an initial damma, avoided in سراة to distinguish سري from ساري.

ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r1.claim: Barara is the plural of bārr.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r1.claim: The Quran reserves بررة for angels and أبرار for believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r1.anchor: القرآن الكريم له خصوصيات في التعبير فهو يستعمل كلمة (بررة) للملائكة وكلمة (أبرار) للمؤمنين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p899/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p899/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p899/r3.claim: The Quran uses البررة for angels because all angels are righteous, while it uses الأبرار for people; the form reflects their relative abundance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p899/r3.anchor: يستعمل "البررة" دائماً للملائكة وليس للناس لأن الملائكة كلهم بررة (كثرة نسبية) فجاء بجمع التكسير، ويستعمل "الأبرار" للناس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r1.claim: The angels are noble, honored by God; alternatively, they are generous toward believers by seeking forgiveness, guiding them to good, and bringing the laws that complete them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r1.anchor: أي أعزاء على الله تعالى معظمين عنده عز وجل فهو من الكرامة بمعنى التوقير أو متعطفين على المؤمنين يستغفرون لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r2.claim: Barara can mean pious, obedient, or truthful in their oaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r2.anchor: بررة أي أتقياء وقيل مطيعين الله تعالى من قولهم فلان يبر خالفه أي يطيعه وقيل صادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r3.claim: Barara is plural only of barr, while abrār can be plural of barr or bār; some say the Qur’an and Prophetic usage reserve the first for angels and the second for humans.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r3.anchor: وهو جمع بر لا غير وأما أبرار فيكون جمع بر كرب وأرباب وجمع بار كصاحب وأصحاب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r4.claim: One explanation reserves barara for angels and abrār for humans because abrār is a paucity plural, which supposedly suits the greater number of pious angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r4.anchor: واختص على ما قيل الجمع الأول بالملائكة والثاني بالآدميين في القرآن ولسان الشارع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says barara is specific to angels because it is more emphatic than abrār, comparing barr to the more emphatic verbal-source adjective ʿadl.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب خص البررة بهم من حيث أنه أبلغ من أبرار فإنه جمع بر وأبرار جمع بار وبر أبلغ من بار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r6.claim: Alusi notes abrār can also be plural of barr and disputes that angels invariably deserve the more emphatic form; another view makes abrār more emphatic and sees human excellence as hard-won through struggle against innate impulses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r6.anchor: لكن قد سمعت أن أبرارا يكون جمع بر كما يكون جمع بار وأيضا في كون الملائكة أحق بالوصف بالأبلغ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r7.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that a skilled Qur’an reader is with the noble, obedient angels, while one who struggles with recitation receives two rewards.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43/r7.anchor: ومن استعمال البررة في الملائكة ما أخرجه أحمد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه عن عائشة قالت قال رسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r5.claim: The angels are honored by God and obediently righteous; barr is the singular of barara.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r5.anchor: ثم أثنى عليهم فقال: {كرام بررة} أي: كرام على الله،

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r1.claim: The angels are honored by God, or kind toward believers by speaking to them and seeking forgiveness for them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r1.anchor: أعزاء على الله أو متعطفين على المؤمنين يكلمونهم ويستغفرون لهم

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih identifies the noble, righteous scribes as Muhammad’s Companions.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن وهب بن منبه {بأيدي سفرة كرام بررة} قال: هم أصحاب محمد

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the noble, righteous ones as angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس في قوله: {كرام بررة} قال: الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r7.claim: Aisha reports that a skilled Qurʾan reciter is with the noble, righteous scribes, while a struggling reader receives two rewards.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r7.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والأئمة الستة عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي يقرأ القرآن وهو ماهر به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r1.claim: The angels are honored before their Lord and obedient.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كرام أي على ربهم برزة أي مطيعين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains that the singular corresponding to the plural barrara is barr, following the Arabic pattern that collective faʿala forms pair with a singular on fāʿil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30/r2.anchor: قال الفراء واحد البررة في قياس العربية بار لأن العرب لا تقول فعلة ينوون به الجمع إلا والواحد منه فاعل

JISHUMI:v10p7284/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r7.claim: Kirām is the plural of karīm, a person of praiseworthy qualities, opposite of mean or base.
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r7.anchor: والكرام: جمع كريم، وهو المحمود الخصال، ونقيضها: اللئيم.

JISHUMI:v10p7284/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r8.claim: Barara is the plural of bārr; birr is beneficial good action, rooted in expansive benefit, as in land and wheat named for their broad usefulness.
JISHUMI:v10p7284/r8.anchor: والبررة: جمع بار، وهذا من الألفاظ التي تجمع الفاعل على فعله، والبر: فعل النفع الحسن، والبار فاعل ذلك،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r1.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r1.claim: Kiram means honored by their Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r2.claim: They are noble by abstaining from sins and raising themselves above them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r2.anchor: كرام عن المعاصي فهم يرفعون أنفسهم عنها , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak’s explanation is that they show considerate concealment and protection toward someone who has been intimate with his wife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r3.anchor: يتكرمون على من باشر زوجته بالستر عليه دفاعا عنه وصيانة له , وهو معنى قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r4.claim: A further possibility is that they prefer others’ benefits to their own.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r4.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أنهم يؤثرون منافع غيرهم على منافع أنفسهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r6.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r6.claim: Barara means truthful and maintaining ties or goodness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r7.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r7.anchor: الثالث : متقين مطهرين , قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r8.claim: Al-abrar are those whose goodness extends to others, while al-khayyira are good only to themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p204/r8.anchor: أن البررة من تعدى خيرهم إلى غيرهم , والخيرة من كان خيرهم مقصورا عليهم

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r10.claim: The scribes are angels: karām means Muslims, and barara means obedient to God, pure, righteous, and free of sins.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r10.anchor: يعني مسلمين، وهم الملائكة { بررة } [آية: 16] يعني مطيعين لله تعالى أنقياء أبرار من الذنوب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r1.claim: The angels are noble in God's sight, or noble through abstaining from sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r1.anchor: ﴿ كرام ﴾ على الله أو عن المعاصى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#14/r2.claim: Bararah means pious ones and is the plural of bārr.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r4.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi accepts that the Companions were noble and righteous but rejects them as the referent here: safarah, unqualified, is a designation specific to angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r4.anchor: قال ابن العربي: لقد كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سفرة، كراما بررة، ولكن ليسوا بمرادفين بهذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r5.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's comparison: a proficient memorizer of the Qur'an is with the noble, righteous scribes, while one who recites with difficulty and keeps at it receives two rewards; the report is agreed upon, with Bukhari's wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r5.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r6.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi explains “noble” as noble in the sight of their Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r6.anchor: { كرام } أي كرام على ربهم قاله الكلبي

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r7.claim: Al-Hasan explains “noble” as keeping themselves above sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r7.anchor: الحسن: كرام عن المعاصي، فهم يرفعون أنفسهم عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r8.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the angels are too noble to accompany a person when alone with his spouse or relieving himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r8.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس في «كرام» قال: يتكرمون أن يكونوا مع ابن آدم إذا خلا بزوجته، أو تبرز لغائطه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r9.claim: Another explanation is that the angels prefer other people's benefits to their own.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r9.anchor: وقيل: أي يؤثرون منافع غيرهم على منافع أنفسهم

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r10.claim: Barrarah is the plural of bārr, following patterns such as kāfir/kafarah, sāhir/saharah, and fājir/fajarah.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r10.anchor: { بررة } جمع بار مثل كافر وكفرة، وساحر وسحرة، وفاجر وفجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r11.claim: Barr and bārr describe one fit for truth; birr in an oath is truthfulness, and the angels are obedient to God and sincere and truthful in their deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r11.anchor: يقال: بر وبار إذا كان أهلا للصدق، ومنه بر فلان في يمينه: أي صدق، وفلان يبر خالقه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r12.claim: He connects the noble, righteous angels with the description of the protected Qur'an and the purified who touch it in al-Waqi'ah.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:15-16/r12.anchor: وقد مضى في سورة «الواقعة» قوله تعالى: إنه لقرآن كريم * في كتاب مكنون * لا يمسه إلا المطهرون
